amendments.rule: **A subordinating conjunction the ASV supplies for a clause whose Hebrew writes none is `added`.** Casuistic law opens its protasis with אִם, with כִּי, or with a waw, and where one of these stands in the clause it takes the ASV's *if*, *when* or *that* by rules 14 and 30: the corpus aligns a waw to *if* and to *when*, and כִּי takes whichever of them the ASV has written for it. But the ASV also writes such a word for a clause that has no conjunction in it at all — *and, behold,* ***if*** *the plague be spread* for וְהִנֵּה פָּשָׂה הַנֶּגַע, and the italic ***yet*** of *he is bald,* ***yet*** *is he clean* for קֵרֵחַ הוּא טָהוֹר הוּא — and there no morpheme licenses it: it is its own `added` unit under rule 30. Do not fold it into the waw that opens the clause, into הִנֵּה, or into the verb, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also* — the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them, and the waw and הִנֵּה already have the *and* and the *behold* the ASV wrote for them. Count the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's subordinators, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s, and mark whichever side is in surplus. **But a coordinator and a subordinator the ASV writes together for one waw are one rendering of that waw, and neither word is a surplus.** Where the ASV recasts a waw's own clause as a subordinate one and writes the pair at that clause's left edge — *And when I looked* for וָאֶרְאֶה, *And when I see the blood* for וְרָאִיתִי, and likewise *and that* and *so that* — both English words belong to the waw's single unit, and the count above marks nothing `added` unless no conjunction stands in the clause at all. Contiguity is the test, exactly as in rule 30: what makes the Leviticus *if* above a surplus is that הִנֵּה's *behold* stands between it and the waw's *and*, so the *if* is written beside those renderings rather than as part of one connective. Head such a unit on the coordinator, which is what the waw itself is; the corpus aligns a waw to *and when* in twenty-seven units, to *so that* in thirty-eight and to *and that* in eight, heading eleven of the *and when* units on *when* instead, so name that competing reading in the note under rule 8. An ASV italic on such a word corroborates it, and the absence of one is not evidence against it, by rule 7.
amendments.why: EZK.2.9 read rule 55's counting sentence literally — one waw in the clause against the ASV's *And* and *when* — and marked *when* `added`. The corpus contradicts that outcome in 73 units: a waw aligned to *and when* (27, EXO.12.13 וְרָאִיתִי → *And when I see the blood*), to *so that* (38) and to *and that* (8). Left as written, the rule would send every later pass to the same `added`, so the counting sentence is qualified where it stands rather than cross-referenced from a new rule. The qualification is drawn narrowly by contiguity so that rule 55's own examples are untouched: in *and, behold,* ***if*** *the plague be spread* the supplied *if* is separated from the waw's *and* by הִנֵּה's *behold* and remains `added`, and the freestanding italic *yet* is unaffected. The heading direction follows the corpus majority (62 units head on the coordinator, 11 on *when*) and the minority is preserved as a note obligation under rule 8.

conventions: The refrain בֵּית מְרִי (2.5, 2.6, 2.8) is rendered attributively throughout, so under rule 28 the construct בַּיִת takes house together with the clause's supplied copula and indefinite article (rules 20, 15) and מְרִי takes rebellious, the unit discontinuous around it under rule 25. Where 2.7 writes bare מְרִי as the predicate, are most rebellious all belongs to that noun: most intensifies the one morpheme the ASV is rendering there and no other morpheme in the clause answers to it.

אִם ... וְאִם → whether ... or whether (2.5, 2.7) is distributed morpheme by morpheme: each אִם takes the whether standing before its own clause and the waw takes or. This is not rule 14's correlative pair, because the second אִם is itself present to carry the second member.

אֵת with a 2fs suffix, which MACULA tags To here, takes with wherever the ASV spends a word on the relation — speak with thee (2.1) and the verbless are with thee (2.6, where rule 49 adds the copula). The unrepresented rulings on אֵת elsewhere in the chapter (2.3, 2.4, 2.7, 2.8, 2.10) are rule 16's ordinary bare-object case, not a different reading of the same construction.

report: Read all 23 candidate groups end to end. Twenty-two are the ASV writing different English for one lemma in different contexts, and the source licenses each: אֶל → to/among/unto/∅ (2.3, 2.6, 2.8) tracks what the ASV writes, the 2.8 s028 case being rule 40's bare indirect object; הַ → that (2.8 s017) against unrepresented (2.3 s031/s033) is rule 41's own limit, since a demonstrative זֶה stands in the 2.3 phrase and takes the one determiner while nothing competes in 2.8; וְ → And/But/or/yet is rule 14's open list; אֵת with a 2fs suffix takes with in 2.1 and are with in 2.6, differing only by the copula rule 49 puts on a prepositional predicate; the two waw+אַל fusions (neither, nor) each have their own present waw and present negative, with no answering member written, so rule 14's correlative clause is rightly not invoked.

The one real split is invisible to the lemma table, which is blind to `added` units: the chapter's policy on English the ASV supplies. EZK.2.3 folds *even* into עַד's *even unto*, EZK.2.7 folds *most* into מְרִי's *are most rebellious*, EZK.2.2 fuses כַּאֲשֶׁר into *when* — and EZK.2.9 alone marks a supplied connective `added`, the *when* of *And when I looked*, although a waw stands in that very clause. Corpus precedent is decisive against the `added`: a waw is aligned to *and when* in 27 units (EXO.12.13 וְרָאִיתִי → *And when I see the blood* is the same shape), to *so that* in 38 and to *and that* in 8. Patched: EZK.2.9 s001 now takes t001+t002, headed on *And*, and the verse's only `added` unit disappears. Nothing else in that verse moves.

Rule 55's counting sentence is what produced the error, and read literally it would mark the surplus half of all 73 of those corpus units `added`, so it is amended rather than worked around. The amendment keeps rule 55 whole and adds the contiguity test that separates this chapter's *And when* from rule 55's own Leviticus *and, behold, if*, where הִנֵּה's *behold* stands between the supplied word and the waw's *and*.

All five BSB disagreements are documented convention differences, not errors. EZK.2.3 הַ ×2: the ASV writes one determiner for עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה and the demonstrative morpheme takes it, exactly as rule 29's הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה → these cities. EZK.2.4 י on אֲדֹנָי: the ASV writes the Lord Jehovah with no possessive (rule 22). EZK.2.8 אֵלֶיךָ: give thee is a bare indirect object, so rule 40 silences the preposition and the suffix takes thee. EZK.2.9 וְ (s003): the ASV writes no connective before behold; BSB puts its connective on this second waw where the ASV's single And belongs to the first, and after the patch that first waw carries And when. None of these edges should move to improve the aggregate.
Three conventions recorded: the בֵּית מְרִי refrain, the אִם … וְאִם distribution, and the To-tagged אֵת. No promotions — the chapter taught one thing and it belongs inside rule 55.
